vendor_company: Descartes Systems Group (acquired Finale Inventory in August 2025)
target_vertical: Multi-channel e-commerce retailer, wholesaler, light manufacturer, distributor
pricing_model: Tiered subscription scaling by user count, monthly order volume, and number of allowed integrations; no setup fees, no long-term contracts
starting_price_usd: $99/month (Self-Starter / Starter plan: 1 user, up to ~500 monthly orders); scales to Platinum at ~$949/month and custom enterprise tiers
free_trial_or_freemium: 14-day free trial with access to nearly all features; no freemium tier
shopify_app_rating: [uncertain] (listed app appears to have 0 reviews / no published star rating as of 2026-05)
shopify_built_for_shopify_badge: [uncertain] (no public indication the Finale Inventory Connector holds the Built for Shopify badge)
shopify_plus_partner_status: [uncertain] (not listed as a Shopify Plus Certified App Partner in available public sources)
shopify_sync_direction: Bi-directional: orders pulled from Shopify into Finale every ~5 minutes; inventory quantity changes pushed back to Shopify within ~5 minutes to prevent overselling
shopify_synced_entities: Products, variants/SKUs, inventory levels, orders, fulfillments; product/variant data and stock levels sync between Finale and Shopify; customer and refund sync handled via order import flow
shopify_service_item_support: [uncertain] (no public documentation confirms native sync of Shopify service / non-physical items)
shopify_multi_store_support: Supported – Finale can connect multiple Shopify stores to a single tenant as part of its multi-channel architecture
shopify_pos_support: Shopify POS supported as a sales channel within the multi-channel sync (POS treated alongside online Shopify orders)
shopify_b2b_catalog_support: [uncertain] (no public documentation describes native handling of Shopify B2B company locations / price lists)
shopify_markets_support: [uncertain] (no public statement on Shopify Markets multi-market pricing / duties / landed cost awareness)
shopify_metafield_to_erp_field_mapping: [uncertain] (no public documentation of configurable metafield <-> Finale custom-field mapping)
shopify_variant_option_mapping: Variants mapped via SKU; Finale uses SKU as the canonical key to align Shopify variants with its product catalog and reflect option-level stock back to Shopify
shopify_real_time_or_batch: Near real-time polled cadence – order import and inventory push run on a ~5-minute cycle (not pure webhook-driven)
shopify_known_limitations: Sync is batched at ~5-minute intervals rather than webhook-driven, which can cause short overselling windows during flash sales; mobile WMS app is Android-only (no iOS); some users report platform slowdowns on weekends and during peak periods; documentation occasionally lags features
etsy_native_or_third_party: Direct integration listed on Finale's marketplace integrations page (also possible via ShipStation as a secondary path)
etsy_listing_creation_vs_sync_only: [uncertain] (Finale primarily syncs inventory and imports orders; public docs do not clearly state native Etsy listing creation)
etsy_inventory_sync: Stock synced across Etsy and other channels in near real-time (~5-minute cadence) to prevent overselling
etsy_synced_entities: Listings (sync), inventory levels, orders/receipts; [uncertain] whether variations and personalization fields sync at full fidelity
etsy_known_limitations: [uncertain] – no public documentation of Etsy-specific edge cases for variations, personalization, or digital products
amazon_marketplaces: US, plus broader Amazon marketplaces via SP-API; [uncertain] exact published list (UK/EU/AU/CA/JP/MX/IN coverage not explicitly enumerated in public marketing)
amazon_seller_types: FBA and FBM both supported; supports Multi-Channel Fulfillment (MCF) using FBA stock to fulfill non-Amazon orders; [uncertain] Vendor Central support
amazon_synced_entities: Listings, inventory levels (including FBA inbound shipments and removals), orders, shipments; [uncertain] settlement reports, returns, and customer messaging at native depth
amazon_listing_creation: [uncertain] – Finale primarily syncs and updates existing Amazon listings; full create-from-scratch listing workflow not clearly documented publicly
amazon_buy_shipping: [uncertain] – no documented in-app Amazon Buy Shipping label purchase (Finale typically routes labels through ShipStation)
amazon_fba_inbound_workflow: Finale syncs FBA inbound shipments and removals via direct SP-API integration, providing visibility into stock in transit and at FBA locations; [uncertain] explicit migration to v2024-03-20 Fulfillment Inbound API
amazon_sp_api_inbound_v2024_03_20: [uncertain] – no public statement on migration status to Fulfillment Inbound v2024-03-20
amazon_settlement_report_handling: [uncertain] – Finale does not natively post Amazon settlement reports as journals; recommended path is to use A2X alongside Finale for Amazon settlement reconciliation into QBO/Xero
amazon_marketplace_facilitator_tax_handl: [uncertain] – not documented natively; typically handled via A2X (Finale partners with A2X for COGS / marketplace tax journals)
amazon_multi_account_support: [uncertain] – not explicitly documented; likely supported via separate integration credentials per channel
amazon_known_limitations: Native Amazon accounting/settlement posting is limited – Finale relies on A2X for accurate Amazon COGS and marketplace-facilitator tax journals; repricing and Buy Shipping not native
xero_app_store_certified: [uncertain] – listed on Xero App Store but no specific certification badge publicly cited
xero_synced_entities: Inventory valuation, purchase orders/bills, credit memos, product data, invoices/sales, COGS journal entries; supports detailed or summarized journal posting
xero_accounting_sync_mode: Hybrid – supports both invoice-per-order detail sync and summary journal posting on user-selected schedule (daily, weekly, or monthly); for high-volume Amazon and other marketplace flows, A2X is recommended for summary journals
xero_cogs_journal_method: Perpetual per-movement COGS journals available; can also be posted as periodic summary journals; landed-cost-inclusive valuation supported via Finale's landed-cost module
xero_tracking_category_mapping: [uncertain] – no public documentation describing entity-level Xero tracking category mapping
xero_tax_handling: [uncertain] – generic mapping of Xero tax codes to Finale tax handling; specific GST/VAT mapping details not publicly documented
xero_known_limitations: [uncertain] – community-reported limits not surfaced in public sources; A2X is positioned as the complement for advanced Amazon / multi-channel COGS posting
qb_online_supported: Yes – native, deeply integrated (highlighted on Platinum plan)
qb_desktop_supported: [uncertain] – Finale's modern integration focus is QuickBooks Online; QB Desktop support via direct connector not clearly documented
qb_app_certified: Listed on Intuit App Store; [uncertain] specific certification badge
qb_synced_entities: Invoices/sales, bills, payments, customers, vendors, COGS journal entries, inventory valuation adjustments, credit memos, purchase orders, product data
qb_accounting_sync_mode: Hybrid – detailed (per-order) or summarized journal entries on daily/weekly/monthly cadence configurable by the user
qb_cogs_journal_method: Perpetual per-movement COGS or periodic summary journals; landed-cost-inclusive valuation flows through to COGS
qb_class_location_mapping: [uncertain] – no public documentation of QBO Class / Location mapping equivalent to Xero tracking categories
qb_known_limitations: [uncertain] – community-reported limits not surfaced in public sources
other_ecom_channels: WooCommerce (native), BigCommerce (native), eBay (native), Walmart (native), TikTok Shop (native), Square POS (native), Faire (supported), Magento (via ShipStation), 25+ channels total via direct integrations plus ShipStation as an indirect channel hub
bundle_kit_component_decomposition: Supported – BOMs / kits configurable with 'Expand vs Never Expand BOM' behavior; selling a bundle decrements component stock and components-on-hand drive build availability
other_accounting_integrations: A2X (deep partnership for marketplace COGS and settlement journals into QBO/Xero); native integrations beyond QBO and Xero are limited – Sage Intacct, NetSuite, Zoho Books, MYOB, FreshBooks not natively documented
bom_support: Yes – Bill of Materials module included
multi_level_bom: Yes – supports nested / multi-level BOMs with 'Expand vs Never Expand BOM' settings
production_orders: Yes – BOM-based work / build orders that reserve components, calculate buildable quantities, and reduce raw materials on completion; routing/operations depth is light (positioned as light manufacturing rather than full MRP)
batch_lot_tracking: Yes – multi-part lot ID tracking with expiry, with customizable validation requirements
serial_tracking: Yes – serial number tracking from receipt to sale, supports bulk imports, GS1 barcode decoding, refurbishment state monitoring
bin_location_support: Yes – hierarchical Location -> Sublocation model (sublocation = bin/shelf/rack/pallet/aisle); barcode-labeled bin locations supported
multi_warehouse: Yes – multi-location / multi-warehouse with transfer orders and per-location stock visibility
barcoding: Strong – generates UPC codes, product and warehouse-location barcodes, GS1 decoding; works with standard Android scanners, Zebra/Honeywell imagers, and thermal printers without proprietary hardware
purchase_orders: Yes – PO creation, partial receipts, supplier price lists, automated reorder recommendations driven by reorder points and lead times
supplier_management: Yes – supplier records, supplier-SKU mapping, lead times; MOQ tracking [uncertain] at depth
landed_cost_support: Yes – landed-cost module allocates freight, duty, and insurance to inventory cost using value, quantity, weight, or volume allocation methods
multi_currency_inventory_valuation: [uncertain] – multi-currency posting to QBO/Xero referenced indirectly; per-currency inventory valuation not explicitly documented
ai_demand_forecasting: Yes – AI inventory management features marketed for demand forecasting, dynamic safety stock, and reorder point recalibration based on sales velocity and lead-time variability
ai_purchase_order_suggestions: Yes – automated reorder recommendations / replenishment suggestions driven by sales velocity, lead times, and reorder points; PO drafts can be auto-generated
ai_natural_language_query: [uncertain] – no public 'ask your inventory' chat-style feature documented as of 2026-05
public_api: Yes – REST API (JSON over HTTPS, GET for reads, POST for writes) with full coverage matching the UI; documented at developer.finaleinventory.com
webhook_event_coverage: [uncertain] – Finale API is poll-based with REST endpoints; outbound webhook event catalog not prominently documented (integrations rely on REST polling and partner connectors)
integration_architecture: Native direct integrations for major channels (Shopify, Amazon, eBay, Walmart, BigCommerce, WooCommerce, TikTok Shop, Square, Etsy, QBO, Xero, ShipStation) plus partner integrations (A2X for accounting, Crstl/SPS for EDI); also exposed via Make community connector
zapier_make_support: Make community connector available; [uncertain] official Zapier connector
mobile_app: Android-only Finale IMS Barcode Scanner app (Google Play) for warehouse operations; no native iOS app and no full mobile UI replicating the desktop app
mobile_barcode_scanning_app: Yes – native Android barcode scanner app supporting receiving, putaway, picking/packing, transfers, and cycle counts
rate_limit_handling_documented: [uncertain] – Finale's own API rate limits are documented in developer docs, but explicit handling of Shopify / Amazon / Xero / QBO downstream throttling is not prominently published
sync_frequency: Shopify, Amazon, eBay, BigCommerce, WooCommerce, Walmart, TikTok, Etsy, Square: ~5-minute polled cycle for order import and inventory push; QBO/Xero: scheduled (daily/weekly/monthly) or per-event depending on configuration
shipping_carrier_integrations: Primarily routed via ShipStation (USPS, UPS, FedEx, DHL, and many regional carriers); also integrates with ShipRush and ShippingEasy; direct first-party carrier connections are limited compared to dedicated shipping platforms
shipping_label_buying: Indirect – label purchase happens in ShipStation/ShipRush/ShippingEasy with order data flowing back to Finale; no native in-app label buying
three_pl_integrations: Supports hybrid 3PL fulfillment models; integrates with ShipBob and similar 3PLs via ShipStation; native 3PL connector list is limited compared to specialist OMS platforms
edi_support: Yes – EDI supported via partner integrations Crstl and SPS Commerce for wholesale / retail trading partners
g2_rating: [uncertain] specific star value (G2 profile is active under 'Descartes Finale Inventory' with positive sentiment around support and multi-channel visibility)
capterra_rating: [uncertain] specific value (Capterra profile is active with generally positive reviews highlighting multi-location tracking, reorder management, and purchasing; criticism centers on mobile app limits and weekend performance)
notable_customers: [uncertain] – Finale markets to growing e-commerce sellers (200-50,000 SKUs across multiple locations); specific publicly named flagship customers are not prominently featured in current marketing
last_major_release: August 4, 2025 – acquisition by Descartes Systems Group announced; product rebranded as 'Descartes Finale Inventory' and positioned alongside Descartes Sellercloud; AI inventory management content and ongoing developer API refresh (developer.finaleinventory.com) are recent investments
owner_parent_company: Descartes Systems Group (TSX/NASDAQ: DSGX) — acquired Finale Inventory in August 2025
last_funding_event: Acquired by Descartes Systems Group on 2025-08-04 for ~US$40M up-front cash + up to US$15M performance-based earn-out over two years
